==Revision History== {| class="wikitable" style="background-color:white;" !Revision!!Author!!Date!!Modifications |- |0.1||Bronwyn Lynch |13 June 2025||Document created |- |0.2||Bronwyn Lynch |30 June 2025||Sent for external review 30 June 2025 {{story|IE570|2}} |} [{{fullurl:{{FULLPAGENAME}}|action=history}} Full History] ==Scope of this Document== This specification establishes the performance, design, development and test requirements of the software for the {{{1|IE570}}}. ==Overview of the IE570== The IE570 Series are stackable Layer 3 switches for Time Sensitive Networking (TSN) and Edge Computing. The IE570 Series extends the Industrial Ethernet portfolio making the IE Series a versatile solution for both access and distribution network. The IE570 series is designed to withstand a large number of harsh environmental conditions such as electromagnetic noise, a large range of temperatures, high humidity, and vibration. This device is fully qualified for use in industrial automation control systems, power utilities, oil and gas, manufacturing, railway transportation (trackside), roadway transportation (traffic control) and many other outdoor applications

Both time sensitive networking and edge computing unit are major integral part of IE570 series, to provide support for time sensitive industrial application with lower latency and security issues. It is fully qualified for Industrial Automation and Control Systems (IACS) in power utilities, oil and gas, manufacturing, railway transportation (trackside), roadway transportation (traffic control) and any installation outdoor. IE570-28GHX series are PoE++ capable with max PoE power of 720W and IE570-28GSX are non PoE series. ===Testing Strategy=== The FRER feature and edge computing model will be implemented at later stage once IE570 is available and will be tested under project listed in feature coverage section. Please refer to the IE050 TPS attached in the reference section ===Security Implications=== Implications are not mentioned in the TPS. Hardware TPM is present refer to https://intranet.atlnz.lc/projects/ATLNZ/Current/3001_IE570/Hardware/Schematics/IE570-28gsx_block_diagram_with_IE050_ECU_rev3_20250729,1).pdf ==Test Coverage== ===Significant New Hardware Elements=== Memory, CPU, 100M/1G/10G PHYs are same as IE560s, updated elements are listed as below: *Broadcom Hurricane3_MG BCM56174 - same family, updated verison compared to IE560 *2 x BCM54901E - Connection to IE050 ECU - testing will be covered as part of https://wiki.atlnz.lc/awpwiki/index.php/Project:3128_IE050_Platform_Support and device availability *POE++ 802.3af/at/bt - IE570-28GHX series - same PoE chip compared to IE360 *PoE input power connector - seperate power for PoE controller *Reset button *Power Buffer module *Hot swappable power supplies (no fans) - IE061-150,IE062-150 and IE063-300 *Alarm ports - RJ45 connector ===Platform Coverage=== IE570 will be tested along with IE570, IE560, and any marvel platform available at the time. This will be incorporated as a part testing to cover broader set of features. Whereas the new TSN will be tested against Cisco device, after feature implementation - YTD ===Feature Coverage=== IE570 series are distinct to the previous predecessor with TSN(FRER) and ECU introduced to allow more time sensitive and critical application along with redundant power supplies. Implementing **secure boot on a BCM56160/BCM56170 (Cortex‑A9–based switch ASIC)** is doable, but you need to design it around how Broadcom switch chips actually work (small internal CPU + external memory + vendor boot flow).

Below is a practical, engineering‑level approach.

***

# 1. What you’re dealing with

From public info:

*   BCM56160 includes an **ARM Cortex‑A9 control CPU** [\[docs.broadcom.com\]](https://docs.broadcom.com/doc/12358308)
*   It’s a **switch ASIC**, not a general SoC:
    *   CPU = control plane only
    *   Forwarding pipeline = separate hardware

### Implication

Secure boot is **not purely CPU-based** — it depends on:

*   Boot ROM (inside chip)
*   External flash (SPI NOR / NAND)
*   Possibly eFuse / OTP (undocumented publicly)

***

# 2. Typical boot chain (Broadcom switch ASIC)

Even without the NDA docs, the architecture is well known across StrataXGS devices:

    [Boot ROM (on-chip)]
            ↓
    [First stage loader (from SPI flash)]
            ↓
    [U-Boot or Broadcom loader]
            ↓
    [Linux + SDK]

### Important constraint

*   You **cannot modify Boot ROM**
*   So secure boot must anchor at:
    *   **Hardware root-of-trust (if present)**
    *   OR **first stage loader validation**

***

# 3. Secure boot options (realistically)

## ✅ Option A — Hardware‑anchored secure boot (best, if supported)

Some Broadcom chips support:

*   eFuse / OTP holding public key hash
*   Boot ROM verifying signed first-stage image

BUT:

*   This is **not publicly documented for BCM56160**
*   Usually requires:
    *   NDA docs
    *   Broadcom SDK support

### If available, flow is:

    Boot ROM
      → verifies signature of FSBL using OTP public key hash
          → FSBL verifies U-Boot
              → U-Boot verifies kernel

***

## ✅ Option B — Software-enforced chain (most common in practice)

If hardware root-of-trust is unavailable, you enforce secure boot **starting from first writable stage**.

### Flow:

    Boot ROM (untrusted)
       ↓
    Signed FSBL (you verify manually)
       ↓
    U-Boot with signature verification
       ↓
    Signed kernel + rootfs

### This is how:

### Step 1 — Lock down SPI flash layout

Partition like:

    0x000000  FSBL (signed, minimal)
    0x100000  U-Boot (signed)
    0x200000  Kernel (FIT image, signed)
    0x800000  RootFS (optional signed)

***

### Step 2 — Use signed U-Boot (critical piece)

Enable:

*   `CONFIG_FIT_SIGNATURE`
*   `CONFIG_RSA` or `CONFIG_ECDSA`

Your FIT image example:

```its
/dts-v1/;

/ {
    images {
        kernel {
            data = /incbin/("zImage");
            type = "kernel";
            arch = "arm";
            compression = "none";
            hash-1 {
                algo = "sha256";
            };
        };
    };
    configurations {
        default = "conf";
        conf {
            kernel = "kernel";
            signature {
                algo = "rsa2048";
                key-name-hint = "dev";
            };
        };
    };
};
```

### Then:

*   Embed **public key in U-Boot**
*   Sign images offline
*   Reject unsigned images

***

### Step 3 — First-stage loader validation

Because Boot ROM likely doesn’t verify signatures:

You must build a **minimal FSBL that verifies U-Boot before jumping**.

Pseudo-flow:

```c
if (!verify_signature(uboot_image, public_key)) {
    halt();
}
jump_to_uboot();
```

Store:

*   Public key hash in FSBL (or OTP if available)

***

### Step 4 — Protect secrets

If OTP is accessible (even if undocumented):

*   Store:
    *   public key hash
    *   device identity
*   Otherwise:
    *   burn key into **read-only flash region** + protect physically

***

# 4. Hardening considerations

## 🔒 Anti-rollback

Include version in signed metadata:

```text
version = 3
```

Store last version in:

*   OTP (best)
*   or protected flash sector

Reject older versions.

***

## 🔒 Flash protection

*   Use SPI controller write-protect
*   Disable debug interfaces (JTAG) after provisioning

***

## 🔒 Chain of trust rules

Every stage must verify the next:

| Stage  | Verifies           |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| FSBL   | U-Boot             |
| U-Boot | Kernel (FIT)       |
| Kernel | RootFS (dm-verity) |

***

## 🔒 Use dm-verity (Linux)

For root filesystem integrity:

```bash
CONFIG_DM_VERITY=y
```

***

# 5. Key challenge specific to BCM56160

### ⚠️ Limited public documentation

Broadcom does not publish:

*   OTP details
*   Boot ROM behavior
*   Secure boot capabilities

So in practice:

*   Most vendors using this chip implement **secure boot at U-Boot level**
*   Hardware root-of-trust (if it exists) is rarely exposed without NDA

***

# 6. Recommended practical architecture

If you don’t have NDA access, do this:

    [FSBL]
      - minimal
      - verifies U-Boot signature

    [U-Boot]
